sections.subtitle: Periphrastic Future (Ir a + Infinitive)
sections.content:
📋 Most Common Future Form

✅ Formation:
• ir (present) + a + infinitive
• Conjugation: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van

💡 Examples:
→ Voy a estudiar (I'm going to study)
→ Vas a comer (You're going to eat)
→ Vamos a salir (We're going to leave)

🎯 Uses:
• Immediate plans
• Clear intentions
• Predictions based on evidence

⚡ Key Point:
Most common way to express future in everyday Spanish (like 'going to' in English)

sections.subtitle: Simple Future Tense
sections.content:
📋 Simple Future Formation

✅ Regular Pattern:
• infinitive + endings for ALL verbs
• Endings: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án
• Keep entire infinitive!

💡 Examples:
→ hablaré (I will speak)
→ comerás (you will eat)
→ vivirá (he/she will live)

⚠️ Irregular Stems (keep same endings):
• tener → tendré
• hacer → haré
• decir → diré
• venir → vendré
• poner → pondré
• salir → saldré
• poder → podré
• saber → sabré
• haber → habré
• querer → querré

🎯 Uses:
• Future actions
• Promises
• Formal predictions
• Speculation about PRESENT: ¿Qué hora será? (What time could it be?)

📍 More formal than 'ir a + infinitive'

sections.subtitle: Future Perfect
sections.content:
📋 Future Perfect Formation

✅ Structure:
• haber (future) + past participle
• Future forms: habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habréis, habrán

💡 Example:
→ Para mañana habré terminado
  (By tomorrow I will have finished)

🎯 Two Main Uses:

1️⃣ Actions completed by future point:
→ Cuando llegues, habré cocinado
  (When you arrive, I will have cooked)

2️⃣ Speculation about past:
→ Habrá llegado ya
  (He must have arrived by now)

📍 Common Time Markers:
• para (by)
• antes de (before)
• cuando (when)

sections.subtitle: Conditional Tense
sections.content:
📋 Conditional Formation

✅ Regular Pattern:
• infinitive + imperfect endings for ALL verbs
• Endings: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían

💡 Examples:
→ hablaría (I would speak)
→ comería (you would eat)
→ viviría (he/she would live)

⚠️ Same Irregular Stems as Future:
• tener → tendría
• hacer → haría
• decir → diría
• venir → vendría
• poner → pondría
• salir → saldría
• poder → podría
• saber → sabría
• haber → habría
• querer → querría

🎯 Three Main Uses:

1️⃣ Polite requests:
→ ¿Podrías ayudarme? (Could you help me?)

2️⃣ Hypothetical situations:
→ Me gustaría viajar (I would like to travel)

3️⃣ Speculation about PAST:
→ Serían las 3 (It must have been 3 o'clock)

sections.subtitle: Conditional Perfect
sections.content:
📋 Conditional Perfect Formation

✅ Structure:
• haber (conditional) + past participle
• Conditional forms: habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habríais, habrían

💡 Example:
→ Habría ido pero estaba enfermo
  (I would have gone but I was sick)

🎯 Uses:

1️⃣ Past hypotheticals:
→ Actions that would have happened under different circumstances

2️⃣ 'If' sentences:
→ Si hubiera sabido, habría venido
  (If I had known, I would have come)

3️⃣ Expressing:
• Regret
• Missed opportunities
• Past speculation

⚡ Often paired with pluperfect subjunctive in 'si' clauses

sections.subtitle: Future vs Conditional: Key Uses
sections.content:
📋 Future vs Conditional Comparison

✅ FUTURE Uses:

1️⃣ Definite future actions:
→ Mañana iré (Tomorrow I'll go)

2️⃣ Promises:
→ Te llamaré (I'll call you)

3️⃣ Speculation about PRESENT:
→ ¿Dónde estará? (Where could he be?)
→ Tendrá 30 años (He must be 30)

⚠️ CONDITIONAL Uses:

1️⃣ Hypothetical situations:
→ Yo no haría eso (I wouldn't do that)

2️⃣ Polite requests:
→ ¿Podrías abrir? (Could you open?)

3️⃣ Speculation about PAST:
→ Serían las 5 (It must have been 5)

4️⃣ Advice:
→ Deberías estudiar (You should study)

💡 Key Reminder:
Both share the SAME irregular stems!

questions.question: How do you form the periphrastic future?
questions.hint: Use the present tense of ir + a + the infinitive of the main verb.

questions.question: What is 'I am going to study' in Spanish?
questions.hint: Voy (I go) + a + estudiar (study). Periphrastic future is like 'going to'.

questions.question: How do you form the simple future tense?
questions.hint: Add future endings directly to the complete infinitive (all verbs use same pattern).

questions.question: What is the future 'yo' form of 'hablar'?
questions.hint: hablar (infinitive) + é. Don't drop the -ar ending.

questions.question: What is the future 'yo' form of 'comer'?
questions.hint: comer (infinitive) + é. Keep the -er ending.

questions.question: What is the irregular future stem of 'tener'?
questions.hint: The stem changes to tendr-, then add future endings: tendré, tendrás, etc.

questions.question: What is the irregular future stem of 'hacer'?
questions.hint: The stem shortens to har-, then add future endings: haré, harás, etc.

questions.question: What is 'I will do' in Spanish?
questions.hint: Use the irregular stem har- + é. Don't use the full infinitive.

questions.question: Which verbs share irregular stems in both future and conditional?

answers.text: All irregular future verbs (tener, hacer, decir, etc.)

questions.hint: Future and conditional use the SAME irregular stems, just different endings.

questions.question: How do you form the future perfect?
questions.hint: Use haber in the future tense (habré, habrás...) + past participle.

questions.question: 'Para mañana habré terminado' means...

answers.text: By tomorrow I will have finished

questions.hint: Future perfect shows action completed by a future point. 'Para' = by.

questions.question: How do you form the conditional tense?
questions.hint: Like future, but use the imperfect endings (-ía) instead of future endings (-é).

questions.question: What is the conditional 'yo' form of 'hablar'?
questions.hint: hablar (infinitive) + ía. Keep the full infinitive like in future.

questions.question: What is 'I would do' in Spanish?
questions.hint: Use the same irregular stem as future (har-) but with conditional ending (-ía).

questions.question: '¿Podrías ayudarme?' means...
questions.hint: Conditional is used for polite requests. Podrías = you could/would be able to.

questions.question: How do you form the conditional perfect?
questions.hint: Use haber in the conditional (habría, habrías...) + past participle.

questions.question: 'Habría ido pero estaba enfermo' means...

answers.text: I would have gone but I was sick
I will have gone but I was sick
I had gone but I was sick
I would go but I was sick

questions.hint: Conditional perfect expresses what would have happened under different circumstances.

questions.question: What is the irregular conditional 'yo' form of 'tener'?
questions.hint: Same irregular stem as future (tendr-) + conditional ending (-ía).

questions.question: '¿Qué hora será?' uses future for...

answers.text: Speculation about the present (What time could it be?)

questions.hint: Future tense can express speculation or probability about the PRESENT.

questions.question: 'Serían las tres' uses conditional for...

answers.text: Speculation about the past (It must have been 3)

questions.hint: Conditional tense can express speculation or probability about the PAST.

questions.question: Which is more formal/literary?
questions.hint: Simple future is more formal/literary; periphrastic (ir a +) is more common in speech.

questions.question: What are the irregular future/conditional stems for 'poder' and 'saber'?
questions.hint: Both drop the 'e' from the infinitive and add 'r': pod→podr-, sab→sabr-.
